subject: Onboarding: VPC/on-prem observability export and collector patterns
messages:
From: Alice Mercer <security@financify.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acmecloud.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability export for on-prem enclave -> SIEM (requirements attached)

Diego / Redwood team,

We're starting the observability onboarding for our on‑prem enclave (Financify) and want to align on acceptable export/collector patterns so we can stay compliant with our audit requirements. Attached is our high‑level SIEM/evidence requirements (financify_siem_requirements_v1.pdf). Key asks up front: 

- We need a design that ensures logs and traces required for audits are delivered to our Splunk HEC (or retained for 6 months).
- Sensitive fields must be redacted/tokenized (PII: SSNs, CC numbers) before any export that leaves the enclave boundary.
- We must be able to correlate traces with request IDs in our system; trace hooks should propagate a stable trace_id/request_id pair.
- Authentication: our security team prefers mTLS where possible; Splunk HEC tokens are also used by the infra team.
- Network: limited egress allowed; we'd prefer pushing to a small set of endpoints rather than wide-open egress.

Can you outline recommended patterns (forwarder vs sidecar vs telemetry proxy), scrubbing options we should consider, and an acceptance checklist for audit evidence? We're on a short timeline — target onboarding window is the 2nd week of August.

Thanks,
Alice Mercer
Security Engineer, Financify
[attachment: financify_siem_requirements_v1.pdf]
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Alice Mercer <security@financify.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export for on-prem enclave -> SIEM (requirements attached)

Alice — thanks for the clear requirements and the PDF. Looping in Kim (security integrations), Marissa (observability ops), and Jonas (on‑prem engineering) to help us land a recommended pattern.

High level options we typically propose (summary to pick from quickly):

1) Customer‑managed forwarder (recommended when SIEM is customer‑first): local forwarder/collector (Fluentd/Vector) inside the enclave -> customer SIEM HEC. Pros: minimal outbound surface to Redwood, full control of scrubbing. Cons: customer owns reliability and replay.

2) VPC telemetry bridge (preferred for regulated customers): enclave -> telemetry bridge inside customer VPC (small egress to a Redwood‑managed forwarder or our bridge endpoint) -> Redwood collects evidence artifacts into a customer bucket for audits. Pros: we can provide hardened receiver with controlled IPs, can centralize replay and MD5 checks. Cons: requires allowing egress to a short IP/CIDR list and agreeing on auth (mTLS + token).

3) Sidecar + queued exporter: run sidecar that performs tokenization and local buffering, then pushes to either (1) or (2). Pros: best for strict PII policies and intermittent egress. Cons: extra infra in enclave.

Scrubbing options we recommend: a two‑layer approach — local scrub rules (regex/tokenization) + a central audit pipeline rule set that validates and drops any PII before indexing. For credit card/SSNs we recommend format-preserving tokenization at source (sidecar or fluent plugin) and storing reversible tokens in a customer‑controlled vault if de‑tokenization will be needed for investigations.

Tracing: ensure request_id is injected at the application edge and mapped to the trace_id. We instrument the runtime to emit a trace header (redwood-trace-id) and add a small shim that copies the application request_id -> trace attribute. We'll include a trace hook spec in the collector example.

Next actions I propose:
- Quick 30m call week of Jul 24 to pick option and confirm network egress/CIDR.
- I'll share a collector-config-example.yaml that shows prom/remote_write and Fluent/Vector examples (attached).
- Draft acceptance checklist for evidence transfer and retention (we'll include log/trace/id correlation examples).

Attaching an example collector snippet for your SIEM team to review.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[attachment: collector-config-example.yaml]
From: Alice Mercer <security@financify.com>

Cc: ops@acmecloud.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export for on-prem enclave -> SIEM (requirements attached)

Diego / team — thanks, that framing is helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- We prefer option 2 (VPC telemetry bridge) — centralizing collection inside our VPC and sending to a Redwood receiver works best for our compliance team.
- We can open egress to a /28 range owned by Redwood; our network team will need the exact CIDRs and fingerprints for mTLS.
- Splunk HEC tokens are used internally; for the telemetry bridge we expect to provide a HEC endpoint for on‑prem -> telemetry bridge, and Redwood to pull/push evidence to a customer‑owned S3 (or an approved storage bucket) for audit retrieval.
- Retention requirement: 6 months of raw evidence; processed/indexed logs may have shorter retention but raw artifacts used for audits should be retained.
- Redaction: CC numbers and SSNs must be tokenized at source; we can accept non‑reversible tokens in the exported evidence, but security will need to understand de‑tokenization process if required for investigations.

Can you include a canary/rollback plan for the export path (how we validate sampling and evidence completeness during the rollout)? Also please include the trace hook mapping example so our tracing team can validate request_id correlation.

Quoted message follows — thanks for the collector YAML, we'll review it and send feedback.

Thanks — good to have alignment. Below is a short mutual action plan and canary checklist we can start with; I've also uploaded the full draft artifacts to the shared Drive link.

Mutual action plan (high level):
- By Jul 21: Redwood to provide exact egress CIDRs, public cert fingerprints for mTLS, and the bridge receiver URL. (owner: Diego)
- Jul 24–28: 30m sync to finalize tokens, auth flow, and sampling targets. (owner: Diego + FinSec)
- Aug 1–8: Canary rollout (1% traffic -> 10% -> 50%) with completeness checks and automated replay for failed batches. (owner: Marissa + FinOps)
- Aug 9–15: Full cutover and retention verification; run evidence retrieval drill. (owner: Jonas + FinSec)

Canary / acceptance checklist (initial):
- Network: Successful TLS handshake from enclave -> telemetry bridge / Redwood receiver; mTLS certs validated.
- Integrity: MD5/SHA256 checksums stored for each bundle, replay test passes for at least 48 hours of sample data.
- Scrubbing: Random sampling (1000 logs) checked; no cleartext SSNs/CCs present. Tokenization matches agreed format.
- Traces: 95% of sampled traces contain both request_id and redwood-trace-id mapping; correlation examples recorded.
- Retention: Raw evidence stored in approved bucket with 6 months lifecycle policy; access logs enabled.

Attachments and links: collector-config-example.yaml (shows fluent/vector sidecar snippets) and the Drive folder with a draft acceptance checklist and trace hook spec.

Next step: Please confirm your network team can accept a /28 and we'll send the CIDR + certs by EOD Jul 21. I'll set up the Jul 24 30m slot and share a calendar invite.

Cheers,
